issues.claim: "Client self-service is a generic upload link, so businesses like yours often have someone opening, identifying and routing each file by hand."
issues.problem: This is an assertion about the agency's internal workflow stated as fact, with no public source. The upload link itself is verifiable; what staff do with the files afterwards is not. It is also the load-bearing premise for the whole of opportunity 2.
issues.fix: Reword as an explicit inference: "the only self-service route is a generic secure-upload link, so in most agencies of this size someone still has to open, identify and route each file by hand — though we can't see your internal process."

issues.claim: Email: "...so evening and weekend enquiries wait until the next business day."
issues.problem: This asserts the agency's process as established fact. The published hours support the inference but do not prove it (they could run an answering service, a voicemail-to-email alert, or staff who work late). Sending this unhedged to the principal risks a factual correction in the first sentence of the email.
issues.fix: Soften to: "...and with all three offices closing between 4:15 and 5:00, I'd guess evening and weekend enquiries wait until the next business day — tell me if I've got that wrong."

issues.claim: "Mistakes here tend to be the most expensive."
issues.problem: Unsourced industry claim about errors-and-omissions exposure, presented as fact. No E&O claims data was retrieved in this pass, and the audit cites no source for it.
issues.fix: Either mark it as an inference ("coverage answers are usually where agencies tell us E&O risk sits") or drop the sentence; the section stands without it.

issues.claim: Impact 1: "Roughly $20,000–$50,000 a year — 0.4–1.0 full-time role at the New Jersey median customer-service wage, loaded."
issues.problem: The two halves do not reconcile. NJ median CSR wage is $47,740; loaded at 1.2–1.3x that is $57,288–$62,062 per full-time role, so 0.4–1.0 FTE is roughly $23,000–$62,000, not $20,000–$50,000. The error understates rather than inflates, but the range and the FTE span describe different things.
issues.fix: Use either "roughly $23,000–$62,000 a year (0.4–1.0 role, loaded at 1.2–1.3x)" or keep $20,000–$50,000 and describe it as "roughly a third to four-fifths of a role".

issues.claim: Impact 2: "Roughly $25,000–$60,000 a year — one role's worth of intake and chasing at the New Jersey median processing-clerk wage."
issues.problem: Label and numbers disagree. One loaded role at the NJ processing-clerk median ($59,810) is about $72,000–$78,000; $25,000–$60,000 is roughly 0.4–1.0 of that role before loading. "One role's worth" also conflicts with a range that starts at 40% of a role, and the 1.2–1.3x loading assumption is not stated in the audit.
issues.fix: Restate as "roughly $25,000–$60,000 a year — 0.4–1.0 role's worth of document intake and chasing, at the New Jersey median processing-clerk wage, loaded".

issues.claim: Impact 3: "Roughly $6,000–$23,000 a year — 15–25% of research time across 0.75–1.5 full-time roles at the New Jersey median customer-service wage."
issues.problem: The numbers only work if a 1.2–1.3x benefits/overhead loading is applied, and unlike impact 1 the audit does not say so. Applied to the bare median, the same sentence yields about $5,000–$18,000, so a reader checking the arithmetic will find it off.
issues.fix: Add "loaded" ("15–25% of research time across 0.75–1.5 roles, loaded"), or state the underlying assumption in one clause.

issues.claim: "Three agency brands — Edison, Belford and Tinton Falls"
issues.problem: Edison, Belford and Tinton Falls are the office towns; the three brands on the contact page are Fraser Brothers Insurance Agency, DeLaurier Insurance Agency and Kennedy & Ward Insurance Agency. As written the sentence labels towns as brands.
issues.fix: Write "Three agency brands in Edison, Belford and Tinton Falls" (or name the three brands once in the opener).

issues.claim: "It fits your existing setup: quote forms and secure upload portal, plus the calendar and inbox your team already works from."
issues.problem: The quote forms and upload portal are verifiable on the site; the calendar and inbox are not. Nothing public shows which email or calendar system the team uses, so this reads as knowledge the audit does not have.
issues.fix: Say "plus whatever calendar and inbox your team already runs" or move the calendar/email assumption into the discovery-session sentence.

issues.claim: Walk-in opener: "I work with independent agencies in Middlesex County on after-hours intake"
issues.problem: An unverifiable claim about our own client base. If we have no Middlesex County agency work yet, this is misleading on first contact; if we do, it is worth naming the pattern instead of the county.
issues.fix: Change to "I work with independent agencies on after-hours intake" unless the Middlesex County work is real and can be described accurately.

issues.problem: The body (headline through "Prepared from publicly available information") is about 465 words, roughly 15 words over the ~450-word cap.
issues.fix: Trim the third bullet of the section 3 impact sentence or the "Why this works" second bullet by one clause; deleting "and a record of who approved what" and "here tend to be the most expensive" brings it under 450.
